subject: Anomalous Fit, Parallel Latent CTT Model using cfa()

messages.author: 326bbae8902de59c
messages.subject: Anomalous Fit, Parallel Latent CTT Model using cfa()
parts:
(This question is from the same project as that which gave rise to my previous correspondence, but concerns a separate issue.)
 
I am fitting a parallel latent CTT model, in which all the factor loadings are constrained to be equal, using the cfa() function in lavaan.  When I test a case with only 4 items, the estimation matches that from Mplus Version 7.  When I fit a model with 5 items, the values of the loadings match Mplus in magnitude, but with opposite sign.  (I also observe this behavior with more items than 5.)  When I run the unconstrained (congeneric) case, cfa() estimates loadings that are similar to one another and the correct sign.  It is not clear to me how I have erroneously defined the model to give rise to this discrepancy.  I am hoping you can help.
 
I have included several files to document this behavior:
lavaan_poll_test_case.R is R code.  First I fit the 4-item congeneric model, then the 4-item parallel model, to demonstrate proper fit.  Then I fit the 5-item congeneric and parallel models to demonstrate the anomaly with the parallel fit.
 
pll_data.dat--the input data for this test case. 
 
lavaan_pll_test_case_transcript.txt--transcript when I run lavaan version 0.5-16 under R 3.0.2 64-bit under Windows 7.  It includes the summary() output for each fit, so that the estimates can be seen.
 
pll_test_case_lavaan_compare_4item.out--output file from Mplus version 7 64-bit running on this same machine, in which I fit the 4-item model. 
 
pll_test_case_lavaan_compare_5item.out--Mplus output file for the 5-item model.
 
Thank you for your assistance.
 
Sincerely,
Lisa Henn
henn...@umn.edu

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Anomalous Fit, Parallel Latent CTT Model using cfa()
parts:
Lisa--
     Signs can be "reversed" (from what is expected) when the factor's variance is set directly--by fixing it to a value like 1, versus indirectly, by fixing a loading to a value like 1.  With the first approach, the Loadings are actually indeterminate with regard to sign.  You can see this in the formula for the variance of an observed variable Y that loads on a factor, F:

Variance(Y) = Loading squared times variance(F) + variance(error)

Since the loading is squared, both positive and negative signs produce the same covariance structure, hence the same fit.  This indeterminacy can extend across the whole covariance matrix of Y, making the signs of the Loadings arbitrary, as long as complementary signs are chosen for all observed variables.

     If this makes you uncomfortable, you can set starting values for Loadings with the sign you want, and that will lead to convergence with the desired signs on your loading estimates.  If you want positive Loadings, set a few positive starting values.  You will need a second pass through your model syntax--one to set the equality constraints that you want, and a second one to set starting values.

Programs differ in how they choose automatic starting values.  Some may impose positive starting values for Loadings as a default, while others may take a different approach.  Trust me, it is not the weirdest thing about factor models.

--Ed Rigdon

messages.subject: Re: Anomalous Fit, Parallel Latent CTT Model using cfa()
parts:
On 05/30/2014 02:50 AM, Lisa Henn wrote:
> (This question is from the same project as that which gave rise to my
> previous correspondence, but concerns a separate issue.)
> I am fitting a parallel latent CTT model, in which all the factor
> loadings are constrained to be equal, using the cfa() function in
> lavaan. When I test a case with only 4 items, the estimation matches
> that from Mplus Version 7. When I fit a model with 5 items, the values
> of the loadings match Mplus in magnitude, but with opposite sign.

Like Ed pointed out: there is nothing anomalous about this. The signs of
the factor loadings are arbitrary.

To give a 'hint' about the sign, you can use something like:

model <- '
Skill =~ v1*item1 + v1*item2 + v1*item3 + v1*item4 + v1*item5 +
start(0.5)*item5
'

(note that I changed the starting value of the last item, since we use
this one when all of them are constrained to be equal).

fit <- cfa(model, data=test.data, std.lv=TRUE)
summary(fit)

gives you positive values again.

Yves.
